segments.text: Good morning class! Today we are exploring the marvelous engine of life on Earth: photosynthesis.
Think of a single green leaf as an ultra-efficient solar panel factory that manufactures food directly out of thin air and water.
Inside every cell of that leaf are microscopic green organelles known as chloroplasts. That's where the magic unfolds.
Now, the overall reaction requires three primary ingredients: sunlight photons, water absorbed by roots, and carbon dioxide inhaled through stomata.
Stage one is known as the light-dependent reaction. Here, green chlorophyll molecules nestled within thylakoid discs absorb light packets.
That incoming light energy is so intense it literally tears water molecules in two—a process we scientists call photolysis.
The oxygen atoms combine to create O2 gas which diffuses out of the leaf. That's the very air filling your lungs right now!
Meanwhile, the excited electrons recharge two vital chemical batteries: adenosine triphosphate, or ATP, and NADPH.
Now we move to stage two: the light-independent phase, commonly called the Calvin cycle, taking place in the liquid stroma.
Even if the sun sets, this cycle keeps turning as long as stored ATP batteries remain. The key enzyme RuBisCO traps carbon dioxide.
Through a series of enzymatic steps, the trapped carbon atoms are bonded together to form glucose—a stable high-energy sugar.
Plants use this glucose to build cellulose stems, synthesize starches for storage, and power their own cellular respiration.
And when herbivores consume these leaves, they absorb that solar energy secondhand, passing it all the way up the trophic pyramid.
So remember the golden summary: Sunlight plus Water plus Carbon Dioxide yields Glucose and Oxygen.
Tomorrow, we will contrast this with mitochondrial respiration. Please review the key terms in your study guide tonight!

keyConcepts.title: Chloroplasts as Solar Factories
keyConcepts.explanation: Plant cells contain chloroplasts that house chlorophyll pigments to capture solar radiation.

keyConcepts.title: Light Reactions & Water Splitting
keyConcepts.explanation: Sunlight splits water (photolysis), releasing oxygen gas and charging ATP and NADPH energy carriers.

keyConcepts.title: Calvin Cycle & Glucose Synthesis
keyConcepts.explanation: RuBisCO fixes carbon dioxide in the stroma, using ATP energy to construct stable glucose sugars.

keyConcepts.title: Ecological Foundation of Biosphere
keyConcepts.explanation: Photosynthesis provides the base food energy and atmospheric oxygen required by almost all terrestrial life.
